subject: Request: executive approval for exceptional Hosted API concession for legacy customer
messages:
From: Erin Caldwell <erin@medforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API renewal — urgent pricing ask

Hannah,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We got the renewal on the agenda internally and procurement pushed back hard on list pricing. MedForge has been a customer since 2024 and this deployment is production-critical across three product lines. Our usage is ramping faster than expected — Q1 billings were $310k and our forecast for H2 lands at $1.2M ARR.

They're asking for a meaningful concession to carry the budget through this year. Can Redwood support a 40% unit-price concession on Hosted API for a 12‑month committed term? Procurement needs either a concession or a firm technical justification they can take to finance.

I've attached Q1 usage and a note from Procurement. Happy to jump on a call.

—Erin

Attachment: MedForge_usage_report_Q1.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Erin Caldwell <erin@medforge.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal — urgent pricing ask

Erin — thanks for the context and for sharing the numbers. I pulled together an initial internal assessment. Short answer: 40% is outside standard concession authority and requires executive signoff.

Quick summary: 
- Current list: $0.08 / token equivalent (hosted).
- MedForge current run-rate: ~$310k last quarter, forecast H2 ~1.2M ARR under proposed commitment.
- 40% would materially change unit economics for Hosted API but would likely secure 12 months of committed spend and expand to two additional regions (US-EAST, EU-WEST).

I'll escalate to RevOps and Sales leadership with the MAP and usage files — can you confirm whether MedForge is prepared to sign a 12-month committed spend + standard data residency SLA? If yes, it strengthens the case for an exception.

I'll follow up internally and loop you back with the outcome.

—Hannah

Signature:
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: MedForge — request exec approval for >20% Hosted API concession

Team,

Escalating MedForge. External asks 40% concession to retain renewal; I recommend we consider an exception with explicit guardrails. Details below and attachments (MAP v3 + usage):

Why this matters:
- Strategic retention: legacy customer (since 2024) with integrated product that will be difficult to migrate off Redwood in the near term.
- Upside: with a committed 12-month term + regional expansion, estimated incremental revenue = $1.0–1.4M ARR (net of concession) in 12 months.
- Risk: 40% would reduce Hosted API unit margin significantly for the term; precedential risk across similar accounts if not tightly scoped.

Proposal (recommended):
1) Approve a 40% unit-price concession for 12 months tied to: minimum committed spend $900k over 12 months, standard SLA, no public quoting of concession, and rollback to list pricing at renewal.
2) Apply quantization and caching recommendations from Optimize (attached) to mitigate token spend; include an opt-in performance review at month 3.
3) Require Legal to include explicit non-disparagement and a termination clause for material misuse (revocation if usage diverges >30% from forecast).

Financial note (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline expected revenue (no concession): $1.2M
- Revenue with 40% concession and confirmed $900k commit: ~$540k realized in year 1; projected expansion in year 2 if retention holds.

Ask: Vivek / Ben — can we get executive approval to grant the 40% concession under the guardrails above? If yes, Legal and RevOps will produce an exec-signed term sheet and get it into DocuSign.

Attachments: MVP_mutual_action_plan_v3.xlsx, proposed_concession_term_sheet.pdf

—Hannah

P.S. External contact (Erin) is ready to sign once she has a firm executive authorization on concession percentage.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: MedForge — request exec approval for >20% Hosted API concession

Hannah — appreciate the clear framing. A few quick thoughts:
- I support an exception given the retention risk, but prefer a slightly smaller headroom: 35% with the same guardrails, to limit precedent.
- Legal should tighten the rollback language and add a milestone-based payout schedule to align incentives.
- RevOps will need to confirm the billing changes are feasible in the accounting cutover window (Q2 close).

Vivek — can you give final say here? If you approve 35–40% I can coordinate legal/finance and queue DocuSign.

—Ben

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: MedForge — request exec approval for >20% Hosted API concession

Team — I reviewed the numbers and the strategic context. I am authorizing a one-time executive concession up to 40% for a 12‑month committed term provided the following are in place before signature:

1) Minimum committed spend: $900k over 12 months (non-cancellable, accelerated billing allowed).
2) Legal to add rollback to list pricing at renewal + a three-month performance review clause.
3) Confidential treatment: no internal or external broadcast of the concession.
4) RevOps to confirm billing implementation and finance to sign off on revenue recognition impact.

Hannah — please coordinate Legal and RevOps; produce an exec-signed term sheet and send to Erin with DocuSign link (upload proposed_concession_term_sheet.pdf). Ben — loop in Marissa for billing.

This approval is limited to MedForge only and does not set broad policy.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Strategy (for the purposes of this thread)
Redwood Inference
